title: Nikon ZR Firmware 2.0 Will Be Available To Download November 23rd
summary: Nikon schedules official release of firmware version 2.0 for the Nikon ZR camera
detailed: After announcing the development of firmware 2.0 for the Nikon ZR, we now have an official release date for when it will be available for download.

sentences: After announcing the development of firmware 2.0 for the Nikon ZR, we now have an official release date for when it will be available for download.
Early adopters of Nikon ZR cinema cameras have been able to enjoy the video-centric tool for over a year now.
But, like all product launches, there has been a growing wish list for alterations that customers have wanted the manufacturer to address.
Thankfully, when it comes to the Nikon ZR, many of the camera’s shortcomings were of the variety that can be fixed with firmware.
Earlier this year, Nikon announced a series of incoming firmware updates for the ZR system.
While a few are still on the horizon, open gate and anamorphic desqueeze, for instance, Nikon will release firmware version 2.0 on November 23 (in the Eastern Standard Time Zone).
It adds support for Log3G10 when users are shooting in the H.265 format.
This is key, as previously, in order to utilize the legendary RED color science, you were required to shoot in the R3D NE format.
But it results in pretty massive file sizes.
So allowing customers to use the H.265 option but still have access to the improved color workflow should be a real advantage.
Especially for those already accustomed to the RED color workflow.
No word yet on giving users the ability to shoot R3D NE files in more compressed versions.
More importantly, the level of noise reduction applied to H.265 footage is now user-selectable.
This is more important than many realize.
One of the key complaints about the ZR at launch was that H.265 footage could appear “soft” in comparison to other Nikon models.
It was theorized that this was the result of overaggressive in-camera noise reduction.
Being able to reduce the level of noise reduction should result in cleaner images straight out of camera.
Focus peaking has been added when shooting R3D NE footage.
Previously, this wasn’t available, which was a big oversight at launch considering many cinema users will no doubt be using manual-focus cinema glass.
Adding this functionality falls into the required category rather than a nice-to-have.
In the nice-to-have category, Nikon has widened the number of operations you can assign to customizable buttons, which should speed workflow for end users.
Starting on the 23rd, the new firmware will be available to download for free from Nikon.
Nikon have never released FW on a Monday, the actual date is 24th around 9am Japan Standard Time.
